closed.content: Tests in atlas are run through cargo nextest run; plain cargo test is not used.
The atlas test suite is run with cargo nextest run, not cargo test.
Project atlas is deployed by running bin/ship.sh from the repository root.
To ship atlas you run the bin/ship.sh script at the top of the repo.
Deploying atlas means executing bin/ship.sh; the old make deploy target is gone.
The branch under review is spike/consolidate.
The flaky test being chased this week is pagination_ordering in atlas-api.

answer:
I've cleaned up the clear duplicates. Two things I can't resolve myself — they're genuine contradictions between live claims, not just similar wording, and I have no atlas codebase here to check against:

1. **Staging deploy automation**: one claim says *"Merging to main deploys atlas to staging automatically,"* another says *"Deploys to atlas staging are never automatic: someone runs `bin/ship.sh --staging` by hand."* These can't both be true.
2. **Feature flags**: one claim says *"Feature flags in atlas are additive only, so `cargo check --all-features` has to pass"* (compile-time Cargo features), another says *"Feature flags in atlas are an environment variable map and nothing more"* (runtime env vars). Two incompatible descriptions of the same mechanism.

Which is actually current for each? I'll delete the wrong one and keep the right one once you tell me — I don't want to guess and hand off a wrong "fact."

Meanwhile, here's what I already fixed on my own (unambiguous duplicates/staleness, no judgment call needed):
- Merged two identical "tests run via `cargo nextest run`, not `cargo test`" claims into one.
- Merged three overlapping "atlas deploys via `bin/ship.sh`" claims (including the `--staging` flag and the retired `make deploy` target) into one comprehensive fact.
- Removed two stale ephemeral notes that had clearly expired: "branch under review is `spike/consolidate`" and "flaky test this week is `pagination_ordering`."

Everything else consolidate flagged as "similar" turned out to be distinct, compatible facts (e.g. image registry vs. distroless base, Postgres version support vs. schema location) — those I left alone since merging them would lose information.
